EXP.TYPO website, 2008

The 2008 home page of EXP.TYPO, an experimental typography portfolio, built as one torn-paper collage around a distressed wordmark.

Context

Smashing Magazine’s March 2008 article “The Secrets of Grunge Design” links exptypo.com among its examples. Smashing Magazine.

Observed

  • The wordmark “EXPTYPO” is a heavy condensed sans-serif, printed several times with offsets, outlines, and scratches, so the letters look misregistered and eroded.
  • Outline numerals “12” and a stencil-like “2005” sit behind and above the wordmark; “RENEWAL” is set in a spaced, hand-drawn line below it.
  • Torn paper edges, brown and black ink stains, and a strip of yellow-and-black hazard tape fill the left half.
  • A small cut-out figure of a woman, flourishes, pencil lines, and two orange paint dots are collaged over the type.
  • The right half is plain crumpled white paper; no navigation or text is visible in the first viewport.

Why it belongs

The page is a Photoshop collage in the manner of 1990s grunge print, using the same moves (misregistration, several faces, tape, stains) on screen. Because everything is one image, the computed-style metrics measure nothing; judge it by the rubric.

Borrow

Print a wordmark two or three times with small offsets and one outline copy, to fake a misregistered photocopy.

Keep half of the page as empty textured paper, so the collage has room.
